# Historical Context
John 3:16 is part of a nighttime conversation between Jesus and Nicodemus, a Pharisee and member of the Jewish ruling council. It is set early in Jesus' ministry in Jerusalem.

# Theological Significance
This verse is often called "the Gospel in a nutshell." It summarizes the central Christian belief: that God's sacrificial love for humanity is demonstrated through the sending of His Son, Jesus Christ, to provide eternal life to all who believe.

# Devotional Reflection
The immensity of God's love is captured in the word "so"—He *so* loved the world. This love is not based on our merit but on His character. It calls for a personal response of faith, leading to a transformation from perishing to eternal life.
